description:
The single largest missing unit operation. crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs/src/ has heater, cooler, heat_exchanger, compressor, expander, pump, valve, mixer, splitter, separator, pipe and reactors — but no column.

SCOPE: multi-stage vapour-liquid column solving the MESH equations (material balance, equilibrium, summation, enthalpy balance), with condenser and reboiler, multiple feeds, side draws and pumparounds. Prefer the inside-out algorithm to reuse the existing flash_insideout.rs machinery rather than writing a new solver from scratch.

V&V per the workspace rule — methodology AND results: validate against a published test problem from the open distillation literature with the reference numbers, tolerances and the measured outcome recorded in the test doc comment.

Enum dispatch for column variants, no trait objects, no Box, no lifetime parameters.
title: refinery: rigorous distillation column (MESH equations, inside-out) in dwsim-libs

description:
Pump (components/pump.rs:14) has only specification: PumpSpecification and efficiency: Ratio. Zero geometry.

Note Pump::evaluate is inert (returns NotYetImplemented, discards its _inlet), though the underlying dwsim free function outram_park_fork_dwsim_libs::pump::modes::evaluate IS implemented and tested and returns head: Length -- but that is hydraulic head, NOT a size. Do not use it for visual scale.

Part of op-dt3.17. The digital-twin widget layer must derive a component's on-screen size from its REAL dimensions; the engine crate forbids new physics, so the dimension must exist here in tampines.

DO NOT use HemSteamCv::get_volume() as a size -- it is the thermodynamic control volume, caller-supplied and unvalidated, conventionally a 1 m3 dummy (get_ref_vol() returns exactly 1.0 m3). It describes the fluid parcel, not the machine.

Prefer explicit named dimensions where shape matters to the drawing; a single nominal Volume is acceptable where only a rough size correlation is wanted. Document units and valid ranges in the doc comment per the workspace human-interface rule, and keep uom types.
title: tampines Pump: add nominal size/envelope dimensions

description:
gh:#57 https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/outram-park-backend/issues/57

Sweep the reactor state — fuel/moderator temperature, control-rod position, coolant density — and programmatically produce temperature-dependent MGXS at each point plus feedback coefficients derived from them, as a MAP over that state space. Then parameterise the map with an in-house algorithm, preferably raffles, so a transient evaluates it per tick instead of re-running Monte Carlo.

WHY THIS IS THE SHAPE THE CODEBASE EXPECTS. genfoam::xs::NuclearDataOneEnergy exposes get(parameters, is_parametrize) with a poly_spline_mode — the deterministic solver ALREADY consumes state-parametrised cross sections and has been waiting for a producer. That settles a design question rather than opening one: the deliverable is a table over state plus a fitted form, not a library at one state point. A transient re-evaluates constants as fuel temperature moves — that IS Doppler feedback — and a single-state library cannot express it.

WHERE EACH PIECE STANDS. MGXS at one state point: MISSING (op-84bc / gh:#42, stepwise op-c1dw / gh:#46). Sweeping a state grid: raffles HAS SobolSampleLayout. Parameterising: MISSING — raffles/src/surrogate.rs is a 54-line stub with no pub items (op-38my / gh:#44). Consuming the parameterised form: EXISTS. Feedback coefficients: teh-o-prke has Doppler, control-rod and moderator-density feedback, but NordheimFuchs is not exposed to Python. Control-rod position as a geometry parameter: UNKNOWN, needs a survey — moving a rod is a geometry change, not a material one.

Two ends exist, the middle does not. Same shape as the rest of this scoping round.

STEPS. (1) Define the state vector — fuel temp, moderator/graphite temp SEPARATELY (op-jyyp.6 splits that channel for good reason), coolant density, rod insertion; say what varies and over what range before sampling. (2) Sweep it with raffles — this half exists. (3) MGXS at each point; fuel temperature enters through Doppler broadening of the pointwise data, so each state point is a fresh RECONR + BROADR + collapse — THE EXPENSIVE STEP, dominates the budget. (4) Feedback coefficients as differences ACROSS the swept map rather than separately computed — falling out of one map is the point, they are then mutually consistent by construction. (5) Parameterise with raffles, emit in NuclearDataOneEnergy spline form. (6) VERIFY by holding out state points and checking the surrogate reproduces them within tolerance — a surrogate without an error bound is not usable for a safety-relevant transient, and this is where the bound comes from.

COSTS TO STATE UP FRONT. Step 3 is n_state_points full MGXS generations. A 4-D sweep at 5 levels each is 625 MC runs with collapse. State the state-point count, particle budget per point and total wall-clock ceiling BEFORE running — this is the most expensive computation in the neutronics scope and a naive tensor grid is how it becomes impossible. Sobol or a sparse grid exists precisely to avoid that.

DEPENDENCIES, one of them not technical: op-84bc/op-c1dw (MGXS must exist at one point first); op-38my (the raffles surrogate — raffles has a NAMED OWNER and adding a ROM layer is their direction call, not a defect fix; this issue is a SECOND consumer for that decision alongside tampines real-time); op-jyyp (HTGR geometry and design point).

NOT IN SCOPE: new transport or feedback physics. No V&V claimed — a map that interpolates smoothly is not a validated map, and step 6 measures fit error only, not physical correctness.

Related: op-84bc, op-38my, op-c1dw, op-wpi0, op-jyyp.
title: HTGR: programmatic temperature/rod/density MGXS and feedback map, parameterised via raffles

description: multi_region::rbf_mapping::RbfFieldMap fits a full 3-D polyharmonic spline; a collinear (pure-axial) or coplanar sample set makes the linear polynomial tail rank-deficient => RbfMapError::Singular (documented + tested in build_rejects_collinear_samples). Add an active-dimension detection that reduces the spline to the spanned subspace so a 1-D axial power profile can be RBF-mapped directly.
title: genfoam multiRegion: dimension-reduced RBF for 1-D/2-D axial profiles

description:
OBSERVED 2026-09-03, and it caused two incorrect public statements before being diagnosed.

The kopi-beans daemon publishes refs/heads/beads/store on its own (CLAUDE.md records this as verified since 0.1.3, kopitiam#19). The daemon's pushes advance the REMOTE ref without advancing this clone's LOCAL refs/heads/beads/store. scripts/push-beads-store.sh then tries to push the stale local ref, git rejects it as non-fast-forward, and the script prints:

    warning: could not push beads store ref to origin; beads remain local only

That message is false in this situation. The beads are not local only — the daemon already published them. The local ref is merely behind.

Impact: during this session the warning was taken at face value and reported twice on public GitHub issues (#17, #39) as 'bead changes are local only'. Both had to be corrected after fetching the remote ref and reading state.jsonl to confirm every change was in fact published.

Suggested fix: before warning, fetch the remote ref and compare. If the local ref is a strict ANCESTOR of the remote (git rev-list --left-right --count gives 0 ahead / N behind), that is the daemon-has-already-published case — fast-forward the local ref and exit 0 silently, or say 'already published by the daemon'. Reserve the warning for a genuine fork (both ahead and behind), which is the only case a human needs to act on.

Low priority as a defect — the script is documented as a non-load-bearing fallback — but the message actively misleads, which is worse than being unhelpful.
title: scripts/push-beads-store.sh: stale local ref reported as a push rejection, misleading callers
